text:
The Rangers' season changed on Oct. 10, when Igor Shesterkin went down with a right knee injury that will keep him out for the year. Since then the net has belonged to Dylan Garand, a goalie with three NHL games behind him last season, and he has held up better than anyone had a right to expect: a .906 save rate and 1.7 goals saved above expected over 14 games. The headlines this week were about the depth behind him. James Reimer was placed on unconditional waivers for a contract termination, and Joonas Korpisalo won his season debut in Seattle. It's Garand's job, and the season leans on him.

The skaters are doing their part. New York has won four of its last five chance battles and taken 58% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in that stretch, yet went 3-2. Sunday in Edmonton was the whole season in one night: 65% of the chances, a 3-1 loss, Devon Levi stopping 2.6 goals more than the shots deserved. The Rangers have finished 8.3 goals below what their chances usually produce. That gap tends to close.

Calgary's problem runs the other way. The Flames have 43% of the chances over their last five and the worst power play in this matchup, at 0.38 expected goals a game. Dustin Wolf has allowed 6.6 more goals than his shots deserved, a long way from the goalie Flames fans thought they had. Joel Farabee has been the bright spot, and Matt Coronato, who won Saturday's game in overtime, sits one goal shy of 50 for his career. Brennan Othmann sees the Rangers for the first time since leaving them.

Our numbers make New York the clear side, 3.2 expected goals to 2.7. Pavel Dorofeyev is our depth sleeper: 4.8 expected goals in his last ten games from a third-line role.
headline: Life after Shesterkin runs through Dylan Garand

hunch.text: Everything points to the Rangers, which is exactly when a goalie with Wolf's track record has the night that turns his season. Our gut says Calgary steals it.
